wholeProduct.summary: TradeScout remains a multi-app local operating system with Scout, Direct Connect, Businesses, Jobs, Community, Share, Exchange, and existing governed routes and data.

deliverables.outcome: A signed-in person can use one stable TradeScout OS shell, start or continue work in Scout, move to a readable Community app, and open Jobs without competing navigation or clipped controls.
deliverables.entry: Open any signed-in TradeScout app at desktop or mobile width.
deliverables.ending: Use the persistent bottom taskbar to move among Scout, Community, and Jobs while each app retains a readable, unobstructed workspace.

proof.procedure: Inspect the three owner-provided production captures for shell hierarchy, first-view action visibility, and horizontal clipping.
proof.expected: One bottom taskbar, compact top-right system controls, no universal side rails, a visible Scout start action, and unclipped app controls.
proof.observed: The baseline captures show a competing top route bar, universal side rails, a missing first-view Scout input, and clipped Community and Jobs controls.

journeySteps: Open Scout and see the primary outcome input without scrolling or taskbar overlap.
Start or resume work while the bottom taskbar and top-right system controls remain stable.
Open Community and read or act on local posts in a full-width app surface.
Open Jobs and use every tab and filter without truncation or horizontal overflow.
constraints: Reuse AppShell, AppShellCore, MobileAppBar, ScoutHome, ScoutOS, and community-feed as canonical owners; create no competing shell, navigation, feed, or Scout input owner.
Preserve every existing feature, route, data contract, permission boundary, Trust/CVS exposure rule, county scope, global browse-only behavior, and Intent to Decision Card to Contact gate.
Keep primary navigation in the bottom taskbar on signed-in desktop and mobile surfaces, with only compact system and account actions at the top right.
Do not push, merge, deploy, mutate production, or alter the separate JW Stone Selective Intelligence lock.

completionClaims.claim: The signed-in shell uses a persistent bottom taskbar and compact top-right system controls without a competing top route bar or universal side rails.
Scout exposes its outcome input in the first usable view and keeps continuation available without taskbar overlap.
Community renders as a readable local app with clear actions and without nested global dashboard rails.
Scout, Community, and Jobs avoid horizontal clipping at the verified desktop and mobile widths.

excludedFromActive: Visual redesign of unrelated authenticated apps beyond shared-shell regression effects.
Backend, schema, routing, permissions, ranking, billing, or production changes.
Push, pull request, merge, deployment, and production acceptance.

deliverables.outcome: Extend verified app-level density and responsive refinements to remaining TradeScout surfaces only when concrete regressions are demonstrated.

executionTarget.rationale: The established TradeScout repository owns the authenticated shell, governed workflows, responsive navigation, tests, and release gates required for this repair.
constraintsConsidered: The repair depends on existing application state, authentication, permissions, routes, responsive components, and repository-level tests.

manualUnverified.reason: The project index was refreshed at the initial base; origin/main later advanced through non-overlapping profile-account and JW changes. Doctor reports pre-existing exact duplicates and owner ambiguity from mirrored exports/workspaces trees.
manualUnverified.reuseDecision: Use canonical client/src and server/tests owners only; do not edit mirrored exports/workspaces copies or introduce new shell, taskbar, feed, or Scout input abstractions.
